title: Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software

pattern_structure.element_1: Problem - The recurring issue to solve

behavioral.purpose: Define how objects communicate and collaborate

design_patterns_detailed.name: Factory Pattern
design_patterns_detailed.problem: Class can't anticipate the type of object it needs
design_patterns_detailed.solution: Create objects without specifying exact classes

design_patterns_detailed.name: Singleton Pattern
design_patterns_detailed.problem: Need exactly one instance of a class accessible globally

design_patterns_detailed.name: Builder Pattern
design_patterns_detailed.problem: Complex objects with many configuration options
design_patterns_detailed.solution: Construct step by step with fluent interface

design_patterns_detailed.name: Adapter Pattern
design_patterns_detailed.problem: Two classes with incompatible interfaces need to work together
design_patterns_detailed.solution: Convert interface of one class into another

design_patterns_detailed.name: Decorator Pattern
design_patterns_detailed.problem: Need to add behavior to objects without modifying them

design_patterns_detailed.name: Facade Pattern
design_patterns_detailed.problem: Complex subsystem with many interdependent classes

design_patterns_detailed.name: Observer Pattern
design_patterns_detailed.problem: Need loose coupling between objects that depend on each other
design_patterns_detailed.solution: One object notifies multiple observers of state changes

design_patterns_detailed.name: Strategy Pattern
design_patterns_detailed.problem: Multiple algorithms for a task, need to select at runtime

design_patterns_detailed.name: Command Pattern
design_patterns_detailed.problem: Need to encapsulate requests for queuing, logging, or undo/redo

srp_single_responsibility.principle: A class should have only one reason to change
srp_single_responsibility.application: Each class should have single well-defined purpose

ocp_open_closed.principle: Open for extension, closed for modification
ocp_open_closed.application: Design classes that can be extended without changing them

lsp_liskov_substitution.principle: Derived classes should be substitutable for base classes

isp_interface_segregation.principle: Use specific interfaces, not general ones
isp_interface_segregation.application: Clients should depend only on interfaces they use

dip_dependency_inversion.principle: Depend on abstractions, not concrete implementations
dip_dependency_inversion.application: Inject dependencies, use interfaces not concrete classes

when_to_use_patterns: Pattern solves a real recurring problem
practical_wisdom.design_philosophy: Start simple, refactor to patterns when needed

benefits_of_patterns: Speeds up development with proven approaches
drawbacks_to_consider: May not apply to specific context
Pattern fetishism can lead to poor design

patterns_not_laws.insight: Design patterns are guidelines, not mandates
patterns_not_laws.interpretation: Use them when they solve real problems
